title: “Blessed Are the Cracked” (another bananasutra song inspired by Bertrand Russel, and Leonard Cohen)
description:
“Blessed are the cracked” is a modern proverb and folk wisdom sometimes (falsely) attributed to Groucho Marx—an aphorism that plays off the biblical “Beatitudes” style, with a poetic twist. It has circulated widely in motivational and spiritual circles, sometimes altered to:
“There is a crack in everything, that’s how the light gets in,” which is a verifiable line from Leonard Cohen’s song “Anthem.” 

The bananasutra lyrics are generally about embracing imperfection, humor, and the cracks that let the light in… and is specifically inspired by the following quotes from Bertrand Russel—one of my all-time fav imaginary down-under boyfriends (ha):

“People's opinions are mainly designed to make them feel comfortable; truth, for most people, is a secondary consideration.”
“Most people would sooner die than think; in fact, they do.”
“War does not determine who is right—only who is left.”
“It is preoccupation with possessions, more than anything else, that prevents us from living freely and nobly.”
“The only thing that will redeem mankind is cooperation.”
“The good life is one inspired by love and guided by knowledge.”
“To be without some of the things you want is an indispensable part of happiness.”
“The secret of happiness is this: let your interests be as wide as possible, and let your reactions to the things and persons that interest you be as far as possible friendly rather than hostile.”
“A sense of duty is useful in work, but offensive in personal relations. People wish to be liked, not to be endured.”
“The world is full of magical things patiently waiting for our wits to grow sharper.”

(Verse 1)
Blessed are the cracked, the broken, the bruised,
The ones who laugh though life’s been unkind,
For every scar’s a map, every crack’s a muse,
And through the gaps, the light unwinds.

(Chorus)
Blessed are the cracked, for they shall shine,
Through the fractures of this fragile design.
A little offbeat, a little askew,
Blessed are the cracked, just like you.

(Verse 2)
Oh, perfect is a prison, a gilded lie,

title: Come Waddle with Me (Penguins in Shoes) • SHOWsutra Cheeky Absurd Chanson inspired by Anatole France
description:
“Come waddle with me” is the cheeky whimsy  flirty Frenchy jazzy sister song of “Penguins in Shoes” (and #unreleased “Penguins in the News”)—a series of dystopian self-help chuckles, inspired by “L’île des Penguins”, an absurdly timeless, surreally real novel by #anatolefrance 

It’s like France rewrote the entire history of humanity… except everyone is a penguin 🐧 And through this absurd, wonderfool premise, he pokes merciless fun at the Church, at politics, at nationalism, at capitalism, at revolutions, at literary pretension—honestly, at everything. It’s a brilliant, potent roast served up as a funny fable.

Penguins are such perfect, adorable, comical tragedians… I mean, hello, they can’t fly. They’re birds, that cannot fly! You tell me a better metaphor for human civilization trying its absolute best #ahem while fundamentally limited and doomed to misunderstand itself? Ha(hem)

Please do yourself a favor: read “Penguin Island”. It’s short, sharp, hilarious, unsettling, and kind—and, a century later, it still explains more about the world than most pundits. And remember to enjoy the wobbly along the way… may we all learn to waddle with joy and #makepenguinsgreatagain

—
Some people ask me how I make songs… and the real answer forever is “it depends”! 

That is the beauty of practicing the experimental art of creativity, it teaches us the paths to happiness are essentially like imagination, i.e. infinite ♾️ All you really need is a brave and open mind, and (more importantly) a curious and gratefool heart.

"Donkeys Years" is a SHOWsutra EP (i.e. where monkeys & donkeys play). It was inspired by a funny party chit chat that brought me joy in the moment—because British humor is deliciously quirky cheeky (like I like), and huh, well, it's just true I'm a hardcore slut for new words and expressions, ha.

This song is primarily about the importance of shaking our rears with no fears aka SHOWsutra fun territory, but(t) it is also very much infused with FLOWsutra + GLOWsutra vibes (i.e. where trust + gratitude shine)… which makes much sense, because at its core, it is (yet another:) thank you letter, and well-wishing lill’ prayer—to music, friends, fun, and freedom.  

--

Desert dust and beachside bass,

“Death is nothing at all. It does not count. I have only slipped away into the next room. Nothing has happened.
Everything remains exactly as it was. I am I, and you are you, and the old life that we lived so fondly together is untouched, unchanged. Whatever we were to each other, that we are still. Call me by the old familiar name. Speak of me in the easy way which you always used. Put no difference into your tone. Wear no forced air of solemnity or sorrow. Laugh as we always laughed at the little jokes that we enjoyed together. Play, smile, think of me, pray for me. Let my name be ever the household word that it always was. Let it be spoken without an effort, without the ghost of a shadow upon it. Life means all that it ever meant. It is the same as it ever was. There is absolute and unbroken continuity. What is this death but a negligible accident? Why should I be out of mind because I am cut of sight? I am but waiting for you, for an interval, somewhere very near, just round the corner. All is well.”

title: Gladys in Sonderland 🍄🐇 SHOWsutra Vaudeville Wonder Waltz True Surreality Story
description:
“Gladys in Sonderland” is a wonder #waltz rewrite of an existential bananasutra song originally titled “Alice and the order of love”… a humanist, empathetic reflection about modern society, which more or less mirrored mirror the great #jacquesbrel song “Quand on a que l’amour”. 

And, in case you’re curious (like me), “Gladys” is meaningfool (to me) because it is my real middle name (a true wonder, for a 100% French girl;), and “Sonder” is a magick word meant to express the realization that everyone has a lens of life as personal, deep, and complex as your own…

—⁠
@bananasutra #songlyrics 

[Intro : Waltz]
The curtain was velvet, the moon a disguise,and Gladys stepped through where the looking glass lies.The floorboards were breathing, the clocks out of hand,and down she kept falling through Sonderland.
They warned her of faith, they warned her of sin,and mocked the light that burned within.So gather, my darlings, the brave and the damned,to hear what she found in Sonderland.

[Verse 1 : The Idol of Romance]
They built their thrones from pain,and crowned their teeth with gain.They swore that great was bright,then stole the people’s light.But hubris blinds the wise,it’s foolish still to pray,to idols made of sighs,those who steal souls away.

[Chorus]
Oh Gladys in Sonderland, look what we’ve done,we sold our hearts to everyone.We trade our grace for borrowed trust,we kiss the gold and call it just.But love that sees, not love that shines,can free the ghosts inside our minds.

[Verse 2 : The Idol of Nation]
They painted flags on bombs,and sang of holy ground.They jailed the women’s wombs,and walled compassion down.But every human bleeds,and every anthem cries,when life forgets its seed,in the wonder of our eyes.

[Chorus]
And Gladys in Sonderland, she understands,we’re building walls with trembling hands.In chasing mirrors, hand in hand,we lose the truth we understand.But love that sees, not love that blinds,unchains the demons in our minds.

[Verse 3 : The Idol of Ambition]
They climbed ivory towers,and reached for golden air.They traded all their hours,for fake-news thrones up there.The higher they ascended,the lonelier the song,for victory’s suspendedwhen you’ve been falling all along.

[Bridge]
Comfort kills the courage meant to soothe;fear makes a god of safety.But sonder, sonder whispers,you are not alone in the ache.

[Verse 4 : The Idol of Self]
They polished up their mirrors,’til blinded by the gleam.They lost a thousand facesinside a single dream.Yet self in love can fly,where selfish hearts must fall;for every “I” that learns to crybecomes the bridge for all.

[Final Chorus]
So Gladys in Sonderland lifts her eyes,love is the riddle that never lies.The truth’s divine, the joke’s on man,we lose ourselves, yet understand:only love that sees, that stands,can lead us home from Sonderland.And Gladys sings her trembling vow:the heart’s a door, be open now.

[Outro]
I’m still falling, still fumbling,still finding the thread of true love through the thickets.But now I know:it’s not how much you love,
it’s how wide your love can see.For sonder is the secret door,and love, the hand that turns the key.

🪄 🕳️

title: How Do Kids Learn Now? 📺 When Did Seduction Become So Untrue? KNOWsutra Flamenco Techno Fusion Music
description:
For 50 years, I imagined most humans on earth shared similar core values—things like kindness and honesty, you know, as if rights & wrong were universal virtues, ha. TBCH, my humble, painful truth is that I still can’t let go of that belief. That’s why I keep asking questions, and refuse to let cognitive dissonance be normalized… Because that belief of mine stems from a deep personal commitment to ethical values that are fundamental to creating a better world, I reckon. And that certainly matters, nah?

Over the past 3 years, unfortunately (to say the least), I have learned my candid belief humans are in essence good, and ultimately, “seekers of truth” (like me:) is deeply, naively flawed, and undeniably, absolutely incorrect. Facts matter and the reality is that people's opinions prioritize comfort over truth, and personal values and principles do vary widely based on their individual experiences, cultural backgrounds, upbringing, and personal philosophies, i.e. their conscious and unconscious fears... 

Please don’t get me wrong tho, I’m a fervent supporter of diversity, and understanding differences in values is part of what makes human interactions complex and interesting, I guess. But(t) I’m not gonna lie, when I encounter situations where it seems like others don't prioritize these democratic values as I do, at all, it feels awfully confusing and profoundly disturbing! And I thank god, i can now make songs to process my anxious grief about the consequences of normalizing deceit as a means to an end—blessed be Blaise Pascal… 

This song asks “when did seduction become so untrue?”, with an emphasis on the importance of kids learning to differentiate rights from wrongs—as required to foster a peaceful, sustainable, harmonious future for everyone. It is yet another invitation to embrace reflection and growth, to help us understand and navigate a world where perspectives differ. It is yet another humble lill’ prayer,  another opportunity to honor my faith, my commitment to kindness and honest, as a core part of who I am (who we are?) as a human, and think about how I/we can positively impact the world around me/us… 

… Even if #robertgreen made shady millions off dollars selling a book that preaches the exact opposite—where “The Art of Seduction” literally means “The Art of Manipulation” aka Deception, where power grab and control matter more than integrity, humility, trust; despite all history, philosophy, economy, sociology, psychology, and of course poetry regarded thinkers agree being vulnerable is being brave, because peace grows from trust, and trust relies on honesty, quite simply!

Lyrics inspired by Bertrand Russel's "Marriage and Morals", where he observed that “Marriage is for women the commonest mode of livelihood, and the total amount of undesired sex endured by women is probably greater in marriage than in prostitution.” (*) And asked: "Are prostitution and traditional marriage interconnected by hypocritical societal structures and discriminatory economic dependency?" 💥

And he asks: What if pr0stituti0n was required as a societal “release valve” for repressed desires, existing mostly as the condemned counterpart to marriage? 

What if the very notion of "ethical paradox" was an absurd oxymoron that never seems to end indeed? I ponder... Why not think of marriage as a relationship based on equality, respect, and personal freedom, i.e. friendship? Could practicing truth, and trust, with humility and integrity, help reduce foul plays--including society’s reliance on femmes de joie, for example, heh? Well duh, d'oh, heck yeah!

Original bananasutra song inspired by the poem “Kindness”—Naomi Shihab Nye (1952). Here’s the original poem:

Before you know what kindness really is
you must lose things,
feel the future dissolve in a moment
like salt in a weakened broth.
What you held in your hand,
what you counted and carefully saved,
all this must go so you know
how desolate the landscape can be
between the regions of kindness.
How you ride and ride
thinking the bus will never stop,
the passengers eating maize and chicken
will stare out the window forever.

Before you learn the tender gravity of kindness
you must travel where the Indian in a white poncho
lies dead by the side of the road.
You must see how this could be you,
how he too was someone
who journeyed through the night with plans
and the simple breath that kept him alive.

Before you know kindness as the deepest thing inside,
you must know sorrow as the other deepest thing.
You must wake up with sorrow.
You must speak to it till your voice
catches the thread of all sorrows
and you see the size of the cloth.
Then it is only kindness that makes sense anymore,
only kindness that ties your shoes
and sends you out into the day to gaze at bread,
only kindness that raises its head
from the crowd of the world to say
It is I you have been looking for,
and then goes with you everywhere
like a shadow or a friend.

title: Kiss a Pulse • GLOWsutra Gipsy Smoky Sultry Psychedelic JAZZ, inspired by Lucille Clifton’s Poetry ✨
manual_notes: the david lynch living room dream
description:
“Kiss a Pulse” is a GLOWsutra (Poetry) song inspired by a luminous Lucille Clifton’s quote I adore: 
“Many people wish to be poets because they wish to wear the title, but one should wish to celebrate more than one wishes to be celebrated.” 

It’s like a tender, psychedelic cabaret dream wrapped in sultry smoke drifting through indie bluesy Gipsy LoFi Dub Jazz, anchored in a hypnotic upright bass that beats like a second heart. The lyrics use playfool alliterations (like I like) and quirky iambic turns, inviting you to taste the sound, blush at the mystery (the deeper the butter:), and let the music move through your marrow instead of your ego—not wearing words, but breathing the rhythm, not chasing vain applause, but savoring plain awe... Blessed be the songs in our bones ✨

—
@bananasutra “Kiss a Pulse” #lyrics

[Verse 1]
So many dream of poet’s fame,
Celebrate names like some lame game,
Wearing words like ego prizes…
But joy is awe, not disguises.

[Chorus]
Who writes the rain, or signs the sky?
Who dreams needing a reason why?
Blush deep, kiss a pulse, hum a song,
Feel the flavors roll off your tongue.

To want a name is not enough,
To love your life, breathe in the rough.
It can’t be faked, to live the beat,
Taste the rhythm, embrace the sweet.

[Chorus]
Who writes the rain, or signs the sky?
Who dreams needing a reason why?
Blush deep, kiss a pulse, hum a song,
Feel the flavors roll off your tongue.

[Bridge]
Why claim titles, rather than dance?
Seek magic truths, imagine chance…
Each breath’s a rhyme, each stumble, art,
Nurture ‘em sparkles in your heart.

[Outro]
Be the poem, feel its grace,
Explore shadows, shine in space,
Forget titles, laughing at thrones…
Blessed be the song in our bones.

description:
This is a #french (my mother tongue) song for those who’d rather be awake than reassured—the ones who’d rather KNOW & GROW than BLOW & SHOW blindly, even if “Some Truths Are Harder to Swallow” 🍌💦  i.e. my BJ (banana joke:) sister-song of “L’Embobinage”… 

The original @bananasutra lyrics are inspired by one of #carlsagan most haunting and relevant psychological insight: 

“One of the saddest lessons of history is this: 
If we’ve been bamboozled long enough, we tend to reject any evidence of the bamboozle. We’re no longer interested in finding the truth. The bamboozle has captured us. It’s simply too painful to acknowledge (even to ourselves) that we’ve been taken. Once you give a charlatan power over you, you almost never get it back.”

“Une des leçons les plus tristes de l'histoire est celle-ci: si nous avons été embobinés assez longtemps, nous avons tendance à rejeter toute preuve de l'embobinage. Nous ne sommes plus intéressés à découvrir la vérité. L'embobinage nous a capturés. Il est tout simplement trop douloureux de reconnaître, même pour nous-mêmes, que nous avons été dupés. Une fois que vous donnez du pouvoir à un charlatan sur vous, vous ne le récupérez presque jamais.”

It’s a story rooted in the #growsutra spirit: a (my) philosophy of fierce compassion, where curiosity is stronger than comfort, where questioning is a form of kindness, and where truth, though sometimes bitter, is ultimately the beginning of healing.

—

“La Force Douce” is the opposite of “Brutal Force”, and my dearest wish is #worldpeace (thank god for sweet dreams ha;)

Artistic expression ain’t a skill, or an asset, it’s a gift! It ain’t about ego, nor fame, or #godforbid money, #corporatebranding or #copyrights it ain’t even really about hard work, nor what buttons one pushes, or what strings one plucks—it is about intentional exploration, about pulling the invisible yet super awesome magic strings only brave pure loving #souls dare to share, as we leap forward, trusting we’re all here to learn aka evolve, grateful we’re all born equal, as divinely mighty as fragile, i.e. #human 💌🎼✨

“La Force Douce” @itsbananasutra #lyrics 

[Couplet 1]
Il faut être bien malheureux 
pour semer la douleur sans raison,
pour étouffer la lumière d’un cœur 
par simple trahison.

Mais moi j’ai vu que la paix, 
c’est pas la fuite ni la peur,
c’est un feu tranquille, 
un courage qui guérit nos rancœurs.

[Pré-refrain]
Ils disent que la bonté c’est faible, 
moi je dis c’est divin,
regarde les rivières: 
elles creusent la pierre, 
sans jamais lever la main.

[Refrain]
Bananasutra 
chante la force douce,
celle qui choisit d’aimer 
quand tout s’écroule autour.

Bananasutra, 
les âmes justes avancent nues,
intègres, vulnérables, 
mais debout jusqu’au bout.

[Couplet 2]
Il faut être bien audacieux 
pour parler vrai sans armure,
montrer ses cicatrices 
comme des fleurs sous la blessure.

Justice, ce n’est pas la vengeance, 
c’est l’équilibre des vents,
où chacun gagne en donnant, 
où l’humain devient vivant.

[Pont]
Quand le monde crie “gagne seul”, 
je réponds “gagnons ensemble”,
le futur n’est pas une guerre, 
c’est un chant qu’on assemble.

L’amour n’est pas dangereux, 
c’est la seule loi qui sauve,
et la tendresse, 
c’est l’arme des braves.

[Refrain]
Bananasutra, dans le feu des jours,
tu gardes la foi, tu redonnes l’amour.
Bananasutra, même au bord du monde,
ta paix rayonne, et jamais ne succombe.

[Outro]
Il faut être bien pernicieux 
pour punir sans comprendre,
mais il faut être divinement fou 
pour continuer d’aimer tendre.

—

"The Gentle Force”

[Verse 1]
You have to be very unhappy
To sow pain for no reason,
To stifle the light of a heart
By simple betrayal.

But I saw that peace,
It's not flight or fear,
It's a quiet fire,
A courage that heals our grudges.

[Pre-crorus]
They say that goodness is weak,
I say it's divine,
Look at the rivers:
They dig the stone,
Without ever raising your hand.

[Chorus]
Bananasutra
Sings the gentle force,
The one who chooses to love
When everything collapses around.

Bananasutra,
The righteous souls advance naked,
Honest, vulnerable,
But standing until the end.

[Verse 2]
You have to be very bold
To speak the truth without armor,
Show your scars
Like flowers under the wound.

Justice is not revenge,
It's the balance of the winds,
Where everyone wins by giving,
Where the human becomes alive.

[Bridge]
When the world shouts "win alone",
I answer "we win together",
The future is not a war,
It's a song that we put together.

Love is not dangerous,
It's the only law that saves,
And tenderness,
It's the weapon of the brave.

[Chorus]
Bananasutra, in the fire of days,
You keep the faith, you give back the love.
Bananasutra, even at the edge of the world,
Your peace radiates, and never succumbs.

[Outro]
You have to be very pernicious
To punish without understanding,
But you have to be divinely crazy
To continue to love tender.

😽🍌

But(t) in reality, his Übermensch is the opposite of what so many believe… he is literally nothing like a selfish, arrogant alpha male figure, nothing like a cowardly, extractive narcissistic villain! And, he is most definitely free of nationalistic, racial delusions; Nietzsche explicitly rejected nationalism and racism. 

His Übermensch couldn’t care less about vanity, power, and wealth hoarding, he laughs at grandiose world (or women) domination fantasies! He’s clearly the opposite of a rich tech bro, sexist jock, populist guru, or conqueror king… He’s bright, he’s brave, he’s fair, and radically #honest

Lyrics inspired by Bertrand Russel's "Marriage and Morals", where he asked: "Are prostitution and traditional marriage interconnected by hypocritical societal structures and discriminatory economic dependency?" 

In this long essay/book, Bertrand fairly observes that marriage often prioritizes financial stability and social status over love, mirroring prostitution’s very transactional nature, and  critiques the rigidity of marital norms, such as lifelong exclusivity and fidelity, arguing it often stifle desires, and lead to unmet physical, emotional, and spiritual needs.

He makes bold statements: “Marriage is for women the commonest mode of livelihood, and the total amount of undesired sex endured by women is probably greater in marriage than in prostitution.” 

And asks brave questions: “What if pr0stituti0n was required as a societal “release valve” for repressed desires, existing mostly as the condemned counterpart to marriage?”

But(t) his point really is this: Why not think of marriage as a relationship based on equality, respect, and personal freedom, i.e. friendship? Could practicing truth, and trust, with humility and integrity, help reduce foul plays--including society’s reliance on femmes de joie, for example, heh?

“Penguins in Shoes” is a SHOWsutra fusion swirl of conscious psychedelic gipsy trip-hop jazz lofi tracks with a dystopian wink. This song was inspired by Anatole France’s 1908 masterpiece “Penguin Island”, a satire so fresh so sharp it somehow still feels like it was written yesterdaze. 

Anatole (i.e. Monsieur France:) took a flock of innocent penguins, accidentally baptized them into “humanity,” and used their bumbling new society to show how fear, vanity, power, myth-making, and herd logic à la ”Rhinoceros” all keep replaying in every era… including ours. It’s funny, it’s absurd, it’s painfully accurate, and delightfooly tender.

I love that tale, because it’s yet another “WTF is wrong with us?” novel, with a sweet absurdist stink of neo-realism in a world gone rotten bananas… It’s a quirky invitation to think, feel, and question authoritarianism, with cheeky, brave compassion—because critical clarity matters, and it’s true most cruelty is born from confusion, most dogma from fear, and most crowd madness from our longing to belong.

And my intention, with this song, is simply to bring a smile to my (and maybe your) day, and honor Anatole’s spirit—goofy, trippy, reflective—kinda like a cheeky little mirror held up to our collective wobble.

So, please do yourself a favor: read Penguin Island. It’s short, sharp, hilarious, unsettling, and kind. And a century later, it still explains more about the world than most wannabe pundits. And remember to enjoy the wobble along the way… may we all learn to slip with jester style 🙏

description:
This song is my RAGGA translation of #BertrandRussell 1929 Essay titled  “Has Religion Contributed Anything Useful to Civilization?” 🚿

If you’re curious, and not familiar with Bertrand Russell’s critiques of the historical and contemporary role of religion in society, his main reasoning points include the following truths:
1. Positive Contributions Are Not Unique to Religion: 
While acknowledging some moral and cultural contributions by religious figures and institutions, Russell argues these are not exclusive to religion. Secular philosophy, science, and humanism have made equivalent or greater contributions without relying on dogma.
2. Obstacles to Progress: 
Russell highlights religion’s frequent opposition to scientific progress, intellectual freedom, and social reform. He critiques its role in fostering intolerance, wars, and dogmatic thinking.
3. Ethical Limitations: 
According to Russell, religious morality often enforces outdated and harmful principles, rooted in obedience to authority rather than rational compassion.
4. Human Potential Without Religion: 
He asserts that humanity can achieve moral progress and meaning through reason, science, and humanistic values, without needing supernatural beliefs.
Russell concludes that while religion has occasionally contributed to civilization, it has more often been an impediment to critical thinking, freedom, and progress… and God knows he’s right!

description:
“Where Wonder Lies” is a sister song of “Question Di Kingdom”, and initially titled “Reason over Reverence”. 

The lyrics are inspired by my sweetheart mathematician philosopher #bertrandrussell and his 1929 essay on Religion, where he asks a fair question: “has religion contributed anything good to society?”…

Bertrand Russell critiques the historical and contemporary role of religion in society. His main points include:

1. Positive Contributions Are Not Unique to Religion: 
While acknowledging some moral and cultural contributions by religious figures and institutions, Russell argues these are not exclusive to religion. Secular philosophy, science, and humanism have made equivalent or greater contributions without relying on dogma.

2. Obstacles to Progress: 
Russell highlights religion’s frequent opposition to scientific progress, intellectual freedom, and social reform. He critiques its role in fostering intolerance, wars, and dogmatic thinking.

3. Ethical Limitations: 
According to Russell, religious morality often enforces outdated and harmful principles, rooted in obedience to authority rather than rational compassion.

4. Human Potential Without Religion: 
He asserts that humanity can achieve moral progress and meaning through reason, science, and humanistic values, without needing supernatural beliefs.

Russell concludes that while religion has occasionally contributed to civilization, it has more often been an impediment to critical thinking, freedom, and progress…

I once read songwriters end up writing the same songs over and over…. And this all means so much to me, I get it now—most of my songs lyrics explore these very themes; this essay alone inspired several songs (or stories, as I like to think of it)!  Here are the lyrics for this one:

Verse 1
They built the heavens with fear in the sky,
Promised salvation but told us to die.
The weight of the world, they placed on their knees,
But truth grows in questions, not in decrees.

Chorus
Raise your mind to the stars, not your prayers,
Build your hope on reason’s stairs.
No need for gods to find what’s true,
The light of love is born in you.

Verse 2
They called it wisdom to silence dissent,
Made a virtue of guilt and a sin of content.
But knowledge is freedom, unchained by creed,
No dogma required to learn how to lead.

Chorus
Raise your mind to the stars, not your prayers,
Build your hope on reason’s stairs.
No need for gods to find what’s true,
The light of love is born in you.

Bridge
No eternal fire, no thrones on high,
Just the vast unknown where truths collide.
We walk the earth with curious eyes,
Finding meaning where wonder lies.

Chorus
Raise your mind to the stars, not your prayers,
Build your hope on reason’s stairs.
No need for gods to find what’s true,
The light of love is born in you.

Outro
So let’s build a world where all can explore,
Free from the chains of the dogma of yore.
For in the search, not the faith, we’ll find,
The beauty of life and the power of mind.


And FWIW, I’m thinking Bertrand would likely approve of this song, because it’s a story that:

• Centers Reason and Compassion: It reflects Russell’s humanistic ideals of building a better world through critical thinking and empathy.

• Critiques Dogma with Humor: It gently pokes fun at the rigidity of religious belief without being dismissive of the search for meaning.

• Inspires Curiosity and Joy: The uplifting tone aligns with Russell’s belief in the joy of intellectual discovery and the beauty of the natural world.

• Encourages Empowerment: The song champions individual and collective responsibility for moral and intellectual progress.

With love ❤️ #philosophy #philosophie #aivoice #sunomusic #folksong

#infrench

C’est un secret de Polichinelle, un histoire que tout le monde connait, mais dont personne n’ose parler. Et pendant ce temps… on recule (pour ne pas dire on se fait encouler ha;)

Cette chanson parle des mots sont retournés, des crimes maquillés en vertu, et du monde qui glisse, lentement mais sûrement, vers une version aussi ringarde que cruelle et dangereuse: un nouveau vieux monde plus autoritaire, plus religieux, plus militarisé, plus masculin, dans le pire sens du terme—un monde ou l’art de la domination au nom du contrôle rend la violence (physique et psychologique) “légitime”.

Un “secret de Polichinelle”, en français, c’est une expression commune pour décrire une vérité que tout le monde connaît, mais que tout le monde fait semblant d’ignorer... C’est le mensonge collectif confortable. C’est le roi nu qu’on continue d’applaudir. C’est le cirque qui tourne pendant que la maison brûle.

Le secret de Polichinelle du jour, c’est que le monde régresse vers une forme d’impérialisme viriliste, fascisant, dogmatique, emballé en “ordre”, “valeurs”, “protection”, “foi”, “tradition”, “bon sens”…

On dit “paix” pour vendre des bombes. On dit “Dieu” pour justifier les maîtres. On dit “ordre” pour exiger l’obéissance. On dit “amour” pour faire avaler la violence…

Bananasutra, c’est l’art de dire les verités d’un monde complètement bananes, de rire pendant qu’on panique, de danser pendant que tout semble s’éffondrer. C’est de la satire tendre et cruelle à la fois... un cabaret politique pour temps de fin de cycle.

Si ça te fait rire → bien.
Si ça te met mal à l’aise → encore mieux.
Si ça te donne envie de questionner, désobéir, crier, et créer, pour le droit d’aimer vraiment, librement → bingo 🍌

⸻
 #inenglish 

“Secret de Polichinelle” literally means “an open (absurd) secret.” It’s something everybody knows, but nobody dares say. And while nobody says it… freaking things slide backwards.

This song is about that surreal moment when words are but(t) excuses, crimes are rebranded as virtues, and the world quietly drifts toward a naughty retro version of itself: more authoritarian, more religious, more militarized, more male-dominated—in for the sheer sake of domination, hierarchy, control, and “legitimate” violence.

A “secret de Polichinelle” is a collective lie of convenience. For example, the naked king we keep applauding... The absurdity of the circus clowns who keep farting while the house is on fire.

Here, the “open secret” is this:
That we are sliding into a new form of imperial, masculinist, fascistic regression, but we package it as “order,” “values,” “protection,” “faith,” “tradition,” or “common sense.” Sigh.

We say “peace” to sell bombs. We say “God” to justify masters. We say “order” to demand obedience. We say “love” to make violence swallowable…

Bananasutra is the art of telling truths that matter in a world gone rotten bananas—laughing while panicking, dancing while dismantling the set… Tender and cruel satire for end-of-cycle times.

If it makes you laugh → good.
If it makes you uncomfortable → even better.
If it makes you think, disobey, create, or love more freely → yass 🍌

KNOWsutra is all about the why… because we must start by agreeing on why #peace matters more than everything, why truth is a sacred, brave and beautiful thing, and lying—or pretending even, omitting for the purpose of selfish manipulation—always a cowardly, shallow, toxic, i.e. wrong decision, which always, in essence, hinders everyone’s safety, prevents mutual trust, and ultimately, #peace #joy and all that the divine offers to all of us humble fools on Earth… 

… her knees are red because she’s been praying—praying we all can GROW up enough to dare being true, kind, fair and respectful, to help each other create a peaceful, grateful, harmonious world #together #withlove 

I created many version of this song, because our “whys” go deep and wide, like my favorite daddies #socrates and #bertrandrussell taught me. Why has many, many shades. Here are the lyrics for this version, with a bonus 3rd verse and outro not included in this audio version:

[Verse 1]
All I know is I dunno, that’s the truth I hold dear
We’ve all got a bit of fool inside, whether far or near
It’s not the clothes, the skin, the job, or the town
It’s not the king or the clown who wears the crown

[Chorus]
It’s the why, oh the why, that paints the shade of fools
Not the how or the what or who follows the rules
In the grand parade of life’s ridiculous school
It’s the why, only the why, that defines a true fool

[Verse 2]
You can be a wise man, still chasing your tail
A fool with a doctorate or a story to tell
It’s not the bright lights or the dark alleyways
It’s the reasons you walk that path anyway

It’s the why, oh the why, that paints the shade of fools
Not the when or the where or who’s got the tools
In the great spectrum of our glorious duel
It’s the why, only the why, that colors every fool

Deep inside, what’s your drive, what’s the spark in your eye?
Do you act from love, fear, or just passing by?
In the theater of fools, every heart plays a part
But the shade of your role is the light in your heart

[Verse 3]
There’s a thousand shades of stupid, a million shades of bright
But what makes you a genius or a fool in the night
Ain’t the facts that you know, or the truths you defend
But the reasons behind each message you send

It’s the why, oh the why, that paints the shade of fools
Not the how or the what or who holds the jewels
In this circus of life, where we all act the fool
It’s the why, only the why, that makes a wise fool

[Outro]
So wear your shade with pride, whether light or dark
In this world full of questions, make your why a work of art
We’re all fools in some fashion, all just playing our part
But the shades that we wear come from deep in the heart

description:
Like all @bananasutra songs, this is not just a song; it’s a story I often tell myself, and care to share—inspired by Carl Sagan, and my GROWsutra philosophy. 

The lyrics are rooted in one of Carl Sagan’s most haunting insights: “One of the saddest lessons of history is this: If we’ve been bamboozled long enough, we tend to reject any evidence of the bamboozle. We’re no longer interested in finding the truth. The bamboozle has captured us. It’s simply too painful to acknowledge (even to ourselves) that we’ve been taken. Once you give a charlatan power over you, you almost never get it back.”

It’s a story rooted in the GROWsutra spirit: a philosophy of fierce compassion, where curiosity is stronger than comfort, where questioning is a form of kindness, and where truth, though sometimes bitter, is ultimately the beginning of healing.

This track’s rhythm mirrors the lyrical flow of Morrissey’s “Some Girls Are Bigger Than Others” song, rewritten into “Some Truths Are Harder to Swallow”—as a smooth but subversive protest lullaby. It feels like a velvet revolt in slow motion, a mellow jazz noir meditation on denial, pride, memory, and the painful beauty of waking up…

My good friend the octopus also makes a quiet appearance here too—as a symbol of memory, intelligence, adaptability, and mystery. Because the real revolution will not be televised. It will be sensed, remembered, grown into. It will happen quietly, in places where eyes are open and minds remain unbought… because, in an authoritarian society, one thing is for sure: revolution ain’t gonna be televised!

This is a song for those who’d rather be awake than reassured… For the ones who’d rather grow than glow blindly, even if some truths are harder to swallow 🍌💦

—
Once upon a time, almost one hundred years ago (in 1930), #bertrandrussell wrote “The Conquest of Happiness”, because he saw ordinary people suffering unnecessarily—not from tragedy, but from misguided habits of mind, toxic social pressures, self-inflicted misery, and other fun facts of classic modern bamboozlism 🖖🤓

Bertrand argued that #happiness isn’t a mystery, or complicated at all. It’s not a miracle. It’s a skill. It’s an experience (with all the little things)… And he gave us a map  🗺️ ✨

Here are my donts & dos lists, my notes about the little things, in 2 songs. This duo-songs EP is my humble quirky silly trippy attempt at translating his map into songs. This is a soundtrack for anyone into being awake, kind, curious, and you know, human… Think of it as a humble and grateful love letter to curiosity, emotional honesty, and the kind of #philosophy  that makes you sit up straighter and breathe easier—with #humor #compassion and a lill’ sASS :)

My hope is that it may entice you to go read more from Bertrand Russel, because his win-win wisdom is timeless—it feels like it was written yesterday, not 100 years ago, and for everyone—I love him so much, and I bet you will too  💌 🎶

—
SONG 1 : “THE UNHAPPINESS DANCE”
A song (x5) songs inspired by the forces that drain joy and distort the mind, i.e. the reasons why people tend to feel unhappy—namely, the emotional chaos, the self-sabotage, and the absurdity of modern misery.

Russell’s #unhappiness list, simplified:
1. #competition — Always comparing yourself to others.
2. #boredom / Excitement Extremism — Swinging between “numb” and “thrilled” without ever landing in contentment.
3. #fatigue — Overwork, stress, and no margin for joy.
4. #envy — Measuring your worth by what others have.
5. #guilt  & Moral Self-Torment — Beating yourself up for being human.
6. #fear of Public Opinion — Living your life under imagined surveillance.

—
SONG 2 : “THE CONQUEST OF HAPPINESS”
A song (x5) about what actually creates lasting well-being, what makes people truly happy. These songs waltz through the antidotes: curiosity, connection, creativity, pleasure, laughter, kindness, courage, and the everyday magic that makes life feel like life.

Russell’s #happiness list, simplified:
1. #zest — Being genuinely interested in life
2. #affection —  Love given and love received
3. #meaningfulwork  — Not necessarily glamorous, but engaging.
4. #wide interest — Multiple passions, not one obsession.
5. #effort & Resilience — The willingness to grow, to try, to adapt.
6. #impersonal Interests — Joy in things outside the self (nature, ideas, art).
7. A Sense of #purpose — Living for something larger than ego.

—
WHY THIS MATTERS NOW?
Because we’re living in a time of distraction, polarization, loneliness, and algorithmic noise that quietly eats away at our sense of self… Because people are anxious, burnt out, overstimulated, overwhelmed, and under-nourished in the soul. And because Russell’s wisdom—nearly 100 years old—feels like it was written yesterday, for the world we’re in right now.

Blessed be George Carlin, and all the brave bringers of truth, light, and laughter.  His razor-sharp awareness of the absurd is a precious gift—not to say a real blessing, ha. This song is part of the GROWsutra (God, Etc) bananasutra collection, and directly inspired by one of his skits with the same title.

In this skit, George points out how some dubious pundits somehow convinced millions that there’s an invisible man living in the sky, watching everything you do, every minute of every day. He’s got a long list of things he doesn’t want you to do. And if you break the rules? Eternal fire torture. Burning. Screaming. Forever. But don’t worry. He loves you, really. But he also needs your money! Ahem. Oh and, he expects you to confess all your “dirty secrets” to single (and maybe horny) holy man in a dark robe, in a tiny dark room, regularly and unconditionally… so you might be “saved”, in the end. Maybe. True story. Sigh.

God knows I’ve got a whole backlog of songs (mostly questions) about religion. I was raised secular, in a country shaped by separating church and state, and by an authoritarian atheist father who believed religion mostly harmed society. So far, based on lived experience, I get where he was coming from… That said: I do believe there’s real wisdom out there. And Hope matters. Meaning matters.

What breaks my heart is the absurd irony: how curiosity gets hijacked into control. How fear gets packaged as faith. How this story keeps looping… again and again. And I can’t help wondering: Is it ignorance?  Is it insecurity?  Is it power? Is it Evil? And, why, goddamn?! Jesus Christ, wtf, whyyy 😵‍💫

Anyway… Praised be critical thinkers, conscious prayers, George’s sense of humor, and the magic of music! #amen

1. get the facts right 
2. keep love in sight
et voilà :)

—
If you’re not familiar with Bertrand Russel, please consider looking him up… amongst many things, he taught me that “People’s opinions are mainly designed to make them feel comfortable; truth, for most people, is a secondary consideration.” And also, that “The Conquest of Happiness” is essentially an infinite, humble game of curiosity and kindness ❤️‍🔥

—
Here’s the fool interview quote that directly inspired this song, when he was asked to outline the advice he would give to future generations, circa 1959: 

“I should like to say two things, one intellectual and one moral. 
The intellectual thing I should want to say to them is this: When you are studying any matter or considering any philosophy, ask yourself only what are the facts and what is the truth that the facts bear out. Never let yourself be diverted either by what you wish to believe, or by what you think would have beneficent social effects if it were believed. But look only, and solely, at what are the facts. 
The moral thing I should wish to say to them is very simple. I should say love is wise, hatred is foolish. In this world, which is getting more and more interconnected, we have to learn to tolerate each other, we have to learn to put up with the fact that some people say things that we don’t like. We can only live together in that way. And if we are to live together and not die together, we should learn the kind of tolerance which is absolutely vital to the continuation of human life on this planet.”

—

description:
For 50 years, I imagined most humans share similar core values—especially values like kindness and honesty, as if rights & wrong were universal virtues. 

Yet, I still can’t let go of that belief. That’s why I keep asking questions… Because that belief of mine stems from a deep personal commitment to these fundamental, ethical values.

Over the past 3 years, however, I have learned my candid belief humans are in essence good, and ultimately, “seekers of truth” (like me:) is deeply flawed, and undoubtedly incorrect. The reality is that people's values and principles do vary widely based on their individual experiences, cultural backgrounds, upbringing, and personal philosophies, or fears. This diversity in values is part of what makes human interactions complex and interesting, I guess. But(t) when I encounter situations where it seems like others don't prioritize these democratic values as I do, it feels awfully confusing and profoundly disturbing. 

This song is part of the EPx16 that crossed the mark of 1000 original tracks released on SoundCloud. So, YAY. I am just sooo grateful for being able to process my feelings with songs. And god knows there is indeed much to process in a world gone bananas. I considered making the 1000th track special, but I’m not that special, really ;)

It is also Vol. 02 of a song I love, “How do Kids Learn Now?” aka “When did seduction become so Untrue?”, a sonic question mark wrapped in 16-track Flamenco Techno journey made of lit Gipsy soul, Arabesk minimalism, flamenco fire, and wonder… asking: What are we teaching? Who profits from forgetting? What is lost when respect is mocked and liberty becomes a loophole?

It is yet another invitation to embrace reflection and growth, to help us understand and navigate a world where perspectives differ… With hypnotic claps, poetic whispers of truth in rhythm, this KNOWsutra release invites you to reflect—not retreat. This song asks questions that matter, with an emphasis the importance of kids learning to differentiate rights from wrongs—as required to foster a long-term peaceful, sustainable, harmonious future for everyone.

It matters to me because my faith, my commitment to kindness and honesty, is a significant part of who I am, and I care to understand who we are as humans, and how we can positively impact the world around us, to make it a better place for everyone… 

In a society where the moral compass is so blurred, covert narcissists charlatans like #robertgreen make  millions of dollars selling a book that teaches the  “The Art of Seduction” literally means “The Art of Manipulation” aka Deception, a reality where power grab and control have come to matter more than integrity, humility, and trust… despite what all regarded history, philosophy, economy, sociology, psychology, and of course poetry scholars know—which is that being vulnerable is being brave, because peace grows from trust, and trust relies on honesty, quite simply…
